why: A site that opens every article with an appeal for subscriptions, written as prose and placed inside the article container, and closes it with a table of index terms. No scorer can tell the appeal from the article: it is several sentences of connected text, carries no links a link-density rule would catch, and sits where the prose sits. The shape comes from a technical news site whose extraction carried the appeal into the archive as the article's opening paragraph, which is what a per-host strip exists for.
title: What the compiler cannot promise you

rules.why: the subscription appeal is prose inside the article container, and the index table is furniture the scorer keeps

must_contain: a type system does not make a program correct
put it where the data stops being someone else's
written where a compiler can read them
must_not_contain: a subscription keeps the next one coming
